results.summary_before: This ASIC implements a low-power pedometer that processes 48-bit SPI frames from an ADXL345 or MPU6050 MEMS accelerometer. It computes the magnitude of the 3-axis acceleration using the Alpha-Max Beta-Min algorithm and detects steps via threshold crossing with hysteresis and a gait regularity filter. The step count is output on eight pins, and a byte select pin allows reading the count in bytes. The design operates at 32.768 kHz and consumes only 656 nW, making it suitable for ultra-low-power applications.

results.summary_before: This project is an 8-bit quantized LSTM neural network accelerator for real-time wake word detection, specifically the word 'NYALA'. It accepts 7-bit signed audio features and a valid strobe, and outputs a trigger signal, confidence level, and busy flag. The design includes RTL and gate-level verification with cocotb, and it requires an external microphone and an RP2040 preprocessor for MFCC extraction. Notable features include a privacy-first smart home application and a fully digital inference pipeline.

results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design translates Morse code entered via a push button into characters A-Z and displays the most recent two characters on seven-segment displays through a Digilent Pmod SSD. Timing rules distinguish dits (1 s hold), dahs (3 s hold), letter ends (3 s release), and word ends (7 s release), with an external LED blinking at 1 Hz to help the user keep time. It requires a tactile switch, an LED, and the Pmod SSD, and includes testbenches for the counting and translation modules. This project appears to be a duplicate of another Morse code translator entry with identical documentation and no silicon test results.

results.summary_before: Dino-7 is a minimalist endless runner game inspired by the Chrome Dinosaur game, rendered on a single 7-segment display. It uses a finite state machine with idle, run, jump, hit, and score-display states, pseudo-random obstacle generation via a 32-bit LFSR, a hardware difficulty selector, and a retained high score. The game is controlled by a jump button on ui[0] and a reset button on ui[1], with optional switches for difficulty and LFSR seed selection. It requires a common-cathode 7-segment display and push buttons, and is notable for fitting a complete game into a single tile with a high-score memory.

results.summary_before: This project is a simple implementation of the classic video game Pong. It generates a VGA video signal through the Tiny VGA Pmod and accepts input from a Gamepad Pmod, allowing two players to control paddles. The design was developed and verified on the Analogue Pocket and in the VGA Playground, with testing done visually rather than with an automated testbench. External hardware required includes a Gamepad Pmod and a Tiny VGA Pmod.

results.summary_before: Wormy is a simple snake-like game where a worm grows by eating and must avoid colliding with itself. It is played using four buttons that are debounced and synchronized to prevent metastability. The game state is displayed on a 4x4 grid of LEDs driven by a multiplexing scheme using eight outputs. The design is educational, explaining concepts such as multiplexing and button filtering, and is tested by observing a moving and growing pixel after reset.
